name: Middle Blue Purple
lede: Middle Blue Purple is a soft, mid-saturation [[blurple]], the X11-list name for a shade the xkcd crowd-survey later called "deep lilac."

sections.title: Two surveys, two names
sections.body:
The name follows ordinary modifier grammar, "middle" plus the parent hue [[blurple]], and our library traces it to Wikipedia's extended color lists [1]. The later xkcd color survey, a 2010 crowd-sourced naming experiment, independently gave a near-identical shade the compound name "deep lilac," a different modifier on a different base hue [1]. Both describe the same patch of violet, from different angles.

Its nearest named neighbor by measured color is [[middle-blue-purple]] itself, almost the same shade, with [[purple-mountain-majesty]] and [[amethyst]] close behind [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a close match in only 2 of 23,781 paintings, 0.01 percent, as photographed; the within-painting lens finds it in 1 [2]. That makes it rarer than 86 percent of the named colors we track [2]. A patch this specific a violet is hard for any photograph of an aged, varnished canvas to hold onto; the scarcity says more about the archive than about how often the color exists in paint [2].
